extraction: Scope-aware. Tracks class depth (`block`/`model` open, `end <Ident>;` close, excluding `end if|when|for|while`) and takes only DEPTH-1 declarations. CDL sources define nested helper blocks with their own connectors — Logical/VariablePulse.mo opens `block Cycle` at line 69 whose BooleanInput `go` is at line 82 — and a scope-blind regex leaks those into the parent interface.
superseded_v1: v1 deduplicated by identifier on the mistaken belief the repeats came from `info` documentation text. They come from nested blocks. Dedup masked nested ports sharing a parent name (u1/u2) and silently failed for uniquely-named ones, recording CDL.Logical.VariablePulse as inputs [u, go] where upstream and our registry both have [u].
independent_cross_check: The consuming test compares 104 non-array classes against the shipping registry on arity and kind, and ASSERTS that count plus zero missing lookups. The other 28 carry an array connector on some side and are exempt: their arity legitimately differs from our flattened form, so they receive NO registry check at all.
drift_check: Port declaration order is identical between this pin and master c4117ccec1f288ee6bc7f0ee0cb40a45d6940b0c: 0 of 132 classes differ.
array_flag_derivation: Per DECLARATION: a side is array only if a depth-1 connector declaration on that side carries a subscript. An earlier revision OR-ed in the registry's width_driven flag, which forced both directions true for width-driven classes and wrongly skipped 12 scalar sides — MultiSum's scalar output y among them.
class_opener_regex: Requires the class name to be followed by a description string or end-of-line. Without that, documentation prose beginning with the word `block` (Reals/Ramp.mo line 127: 'block has the boolean input ...') is parsed as a class opening and corrupts depth tracking.
